blocks.content: The expansion of British power in India was one of the most significant developments in Indian history. The British East India Company gradually transformed from a trading company into a political power.
1. Background of British Expansion
• The English East India Company was established in 1600.
• Initially the company came to India for trade.
• Gradually the British began interfering in Indian politics.
• The decline of the Mughal Empire created opportunities for British expansion.
2. Battle of Plassey (1757)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Battle of Plassey (1757) initiated the foundation of British political presence in Bengal.
The victory in the Battle of Buxar (1764) resulted in the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), formalizing British revenue-collecting power.
The British utilized administrative mechanisms such as the Subsidiary Alliance and Doctrine of Lapse for territorial acquisition.
Key Governors-General shaped economic policies that fundamentally altered India's agrarian and commercial framework.

blocks.content: • Fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah.
• Robert Clive led the British forces.
• Mir Jafar betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah and supported the British.
• The battle took place on 23 June 1757.
• The British victory marked the beginning of British political power in India.
3. Battle of Buxar (1764)
• Fought between the British and a combined force of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II.
• The battle took place on 22 October 1764.
• The British army was led by Hector Munro.
• The British victory strengthened their control over Bengal.
4. Treaty of Allahabad (1765)
• Signed between Robert Clive and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
• The British obtained the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
• This allowed the British to collect revenue from these regions.
5. Subsidiary Alliance
• Introduced by Lord Wellesley.
• Indian rulers had to accept British troops within their territories.
• The ruler had to pay for the maintenance of the British army.
• Without British permission they could not enter alliances with other powers.
6. Doctrine of Lapse

rows: Established British political influence in Bengal
Consolidated British military supremacy over Indian rulers
Granted revenue collection rights (Diwani) to the East India Company

blocks.content: • Introduced by Lord Dalhousie.
• If a ruler died without a natural heir, the kingdom would be annexed by the British.
• Important states annexed: Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur.
7. Important Governors-General
8. Economic Policies of the British
• Heavy land revenue policies were imposed.
• Indian handicraft industries declined.
• Raw materials were exported to Britain.
• India became a market for British manufactured goods.
9. Impact of British Expansion
• Decline of traditional Indian industries.
• Expansion of British political control.

items: Memorize the chronological sequence: Battle of Plassey (1757) followed by Battle of Buxar (1764) and the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
Understand the key differences and proponents behind the Subsidiary Alliance and the Doctrine of Lapse.
Review important Governors-General and their economic policies as they are regularly featured in competitive and Banking exams.

• Beginning of modern administrative systems.

• Robert Clive played a major role in establishing British power in India.
